items.title: Phishing emails pose as Microsoft 365 outage notices to steal logins
items.why: Microsoft says attackers are sending fake outage alerts to US organizations after this week's Microsoft 365 disruption, claiming held emails will be deleted in 24 hours unless the recipient clicks to restore them.
items.action: Warn staff that Microsoft never asks them to click to restore held mail, and have IT search for subject lines starting with 'Outage -' and block the links.

items.title: FBI warns attackers are using the ARTEX AI tool to break into networks in hours
items.why: An FBI flash alert says several hacking groups use ARTEX, an open-source AI attack framework, to automate scanning, break-ins and data theft, sometimes reaching admin access in under three hours. Victims span finance, health care and tech.
items.action: Review internet-facing apps and third-party integrations, limit who can reach cloud admin consoles, and set alerts for new admin accounts or sudden privilege changes.

items.title: Cursor details breach behind fake Claude Code update: a vendor's leaked AI key
items.why: Cursor says an attacker used a key exposed by its AI vendor Fireworks to copy coding session data, then reached support emails, contact details and some credentials. The same vendor breach also hit Uber and Notion.
items.action: Rotate any API keys or passwords your developers pasted into Cursor or sent to its support, and list which AI vendors hold copies of your data.

items.title: Attackers guess passwords on exposed SQL Servers to plant miners and backdoors
items.why: FortiGuard Labs says a campaign running since October scans for SQL Server on port 1433, tries over 2,700 passwords against accounts like 'sa', then installs a crypto miner and a Gh0st RAT backdoor.
items.action: Block port 1433 from the internet, give the sa account a long unique password or disable it, and turn off xp_cmdshell unless you need it.

items.title: Accounting firm Baker Tilly says client SSNs were stolen through a vendor's platform
items.why: Hackers took names and Social Security numbers of clients and their dependents from a platform run by one of the firm's service providers in September. Texas filings alone show more than 10,000 people affected.
items.action: Ask your accountant and payroll provider which outside platforms hold your staff and client tax data, and watch for notification letters this month.

items.title: PostgreSQL fixes 52 flaws, including bugs that let a database user run server code
items.why: New releases for versions 14 through 18 fix 52 issues; the worst let a user who can create objects run commands on the server, and one lets anyone restart version 18. No attacks reported yet.
items.action: Update PostgreSQL to 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 or 14.25, rebuild extensions at the same time, and plan off version 14, which has now reached end of life.
